name: Lying Leg Raise
summary: A supine bodyweight abdominal exercise that involves raising extended legs toward vertical while resisting lumbar extension.

setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat or flat bench with your legs fully extended and together.
Place your arms along your sides with palms pressing into the surface, or lightly grip the sides of the bench overhead for stability.
Posteriorly tilt your pelvis to press your lower back firmly into the floor or bench.
steps: Brace your core and slowly lift both legs together, keeping your knees extended or with a minimal soft bend.
Raise your legs until they form an angle roughly perpendicular to your torso, allowing the pelvis to slightly curl upward at the top for maximum abdominal contraction.
Slowly lower your legs under control back toward the floor, stopping just before your heels touch or before your lower back begins to arch.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower your legs toward the floor; exhale forcefully as you raise them back up.
cues: Keep your lower back glued to the floor.
Pull with your lower abs, not just your hip flexors.
Control the descent; do not drop your legs.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the lower back to arch excessively off the floor during the descent.
common_faults.correction: Only lower your legs as far as you can maintain a flat lower back; bend the knees slightly to reduce lever length if needed.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the legs up rapidly using momentum.
common_faults.correction: Perform the movement slowly, initiating the pull from the abdominals and hip flexors with a distinct pause at the top.

precautions: Avoid this movement if it provokes sharp lower-back discomfort; regress to bent-knee raises to shorten the lever arm.
